properties.name: "reflow2 DOES NO NETWORK I/O, by principle" is a sentence in a deferred idea's pushback, not an accepted rule, and it has been untrue since the remote client
properties.statement: Checked while building chg:an-exposed-server-verifies-bearer-tokens-itself (#616 fix 4, bearer half), which fetches an issuer's key set over the network. The only statement in the design that forbids network I/O is the pushback in dec:idea-open-design-items-become-jira-tasks (status deferred): "reflow2 DOES NO NETWORK I/O, by principle. The Jira call belongs to the agent, a script or flo2, never inside reflow2 itself." No accepted Requirement, Decision or DesignRule says so. req:reflow2-keeps-working-entirely-on-one-machine (accepted) asks that LOCAL use needs no network, which still holds: nothing is fetched unless an operator names an issuer. And reflow2 already reaches the network on a person's or operator's word: the --remote client (req:a-local-client-works-against-a-remote-reflow2-server-by-url) and a watched design's fingerprint (ReflowService::reaches_out). The line the code actually draws is that a server never reaches an address a CALLER supplied (a registry sets without_reaching_out); the bearer verifier keeps it — the issuer, key set URL or file come only from the operator, and a token's jku/x5u/jwk headers are never followed. FOR ANTHONY: the sentence reads like a principle and is not one. Either retire it, or state the real rule (no network I/O on a caller's say-so; local use needs none) as a DesignRule.
